subject: Re: Deployment mode — performance criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@nimbushealth.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode — performance criteria & next steps

Hi Amit / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the patient-facing inference use case. Quick recap and a few items we need to lock down to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated (or Private) for Nimbus. I've attached the sample metrics you shared and a short MOP draft for a perf pilot.

What we heard on the call:
- Target latency: P95 <= 80 ms, P99 <= 150 ms for short prompts (~128 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 250 requests/sec during peak windows (30–45 min bursts up to ~600 rps).
- Model footprint: using a 13B model (quantized) with KV cache hits on repeated prompts.
- Data residency: US-only; no on-prem requirement today but SOC2 & audit logs required.

Initial guidance:
- Hosted API (standard) gives fastest onboarding but may need to be routed to a Dedicated pool if you need guaranteed throughput and isolation.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) is the best fit if 250 sustained rps with tight P99 SLAs is mandatory — we can size a pool to meet 250–600 rps with predictable latency.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is optional if you later require air-gapped operations.

Can you confirm the P95/P99 targets above and share a short sample of your traffic shape (attached CSV looked helpful)? Also confirm whether you need billing/commit predictability (monthly committed spend) vs. pay-as-you-go.

Next steps I propose:
1) Nimbus shares a 24-hour sample traffic CSV (if available) — I attached what you sent during the call.
2) Redwood runs a 2-hour pilot on a Dedicated staging pool (we'll propose sizing once we have traffic shape).
3) We map cost delta between Hosted with burst protections vs Dedicated reserved.

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Engineering (Dylan) to scope the perf run and Lauren for contractual/commit questions.

Best,
Jonas
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 11 May 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode — performance criteria & next steps

Jonas — thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- P95 target is firm at <= 80ms. P99 is a soft target; anything under 200ms is acceptable during short bursts.
- Throughput: the 250 rps is steady for our east-coast peak; spikes up to ~600 rps are expected during certain campaign events (3–4x per week).
- Models: primary model is a quantized 13B as mentioned; we may use a smaller 7B for lower-cost fallbacks for non-critical responses.
- Compliance: SOC2 is mandatory; we also need 13 months of audit logs and a simple export for our privacy team.

Questions:
1) For the Dedicated pilot, can you simulate both sustained load and spike patterns so we can see tail latency behaviour?
2) How fast can you set up a Dedicated pool for a staging pilot (estimate in hours/days)?
3) Can you provide a back-of-envelope cost comparison (per-1M tokens) for Hosted vs Dedicated sizing that meets these numbers?

Cc'ing Priya (Product) to keep her in the loop. We'd like a decision by the end of next week if possible.

Thanks,
Amit
Head of Product, Nimbus Health
amit.shah@nimbushealth.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Deployment mode — performance criteria & next steps (internal)

Internal note / proposed plan:

Jonas — based on Nimbus targets here are pragmatic options we can present:

Option A — Hosted + burst routing (lowest initial friction)
- Pros: immediate onboarding, no reserved commit up-front.
- Cons: may see higher P99 under sustained spikes; cost variable.
- When to pick: if Nimbus values time-to-live and wants to test without commit.

Option B — Dedicated reserved pool (recommended if P95 SLA is required)
- Baseline sizing: 4 x A100-L (or cloud equivalent) for sustained 250 rps with P95 ~60–80ms; supports spikes up to ~600 rps with autoscaling/bursting policies.
- Pilot: 2-hour sustained run + 15m simulated spikes; run in staging region (US-east) to match latency.
- Ops: we can provision staging Dedicated in ~24–48 hours if infra approvals are green; production-grade reserved deployment ~5 business days including routing and alert configs.
- Estimated delta: ~20–35% higher fixed monthly cost vs pure pay-as-you-go in heavy sustained workloads but lowers per-token cost under steady load.

Option C — Private VPC (only if Nimbus needs on-prem or stricter network controls)
- Not necessary based on current answers; keep as future path.

Action items (internal):
- Jonas: confirm pilot window and owners with Nimbus.
- Dylan: prepare pilot runbook + load generator configs (I'll attach draft).
- Lauren: prepare an example reserved pricing term (monthly commit) and a PS SOW template.

I attached a draft MOP (routing/caching knobs and metrics to capture).

-D
Dylan Brooks
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

Amit / Priya — thanks for the fast reply and the decision window. Quick summary and proposed calendar: 

Confirmed: P95 <= 80ms (firm), P99 soft target <= 200ms; sustained 250 rps, spikes up to 600 rps. SOC2 + 13 months logs required.

Proposed pilot plan:
- Redwood runs a 2-hour Dedicated staging run (US-east) with:
  - 2 hours sustained at 250 rps,
  - 3x short spikes to 600 rps (15m each) to observe tail latency,
  - Collect P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU util, KV cache hit-rate, and end-to-end response time.
- Timeline: provision staging Dedicated within 24–48 hours; pilot start as early as Monday 18 May if that works.
- Deliverables: pilot report + cost model comparing Hosted (with burst routing) vs Dedicated reserved for your steady-state.

Questions for you (please confirm by EOD Fri):
1) Is Monday 18 May acceptable for a pilot (we'll aim to provision Friday if green)?
2) Please re-share any sample traffic (CSV) with timestamps in UTC so we can tune generators — the attached CSV was helpful but missing a timezone column.
3) Any legal/compliance contacts we should include now for SOC2 scope?

If you confirm, Dylan will post the runbook and Lauren will follow up with pricing/term options.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scoped.

Jonas
